chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abd al-Malik ibn Amr, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say about the sacrifices of the Christians?' He said, 'There is no harm in them.' I said, 'For they mention the Messiah over them.' He said, 'They only meant God by the Messiah.'

key_terms.ذَبَائِحِ: Sacrifices (animals slaughtered for food or ritual)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Are Christian sacrifices considered halal for Shia Muslims?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms the permissibility of consuming Christian sacrifices, resolving the theological concern regarding their invocation of 'the Messiah' by interpreting it as a reference to God. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and the general permissibility of *Ahl al-Kitab* food, provided the specific act of major shirk is not explicitly tied to the meat's impurity. It highlights the pragmatic approach of the Imams in distinguishing between linguistic usage and theological essence in interfaith dietary laws.
